Title: Trace join reports orphans
Requirement: trace.py shall join the SN->SR->LLR->TC registries and, with --strict, exit nonzero if any orphan exists.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 — a hand-asserted trace is a claim, not evidence: with no mechanical join an SR can lose its last test and nothing reports it, so a gate passes on a spine that no longer holds. Reviewing the matrix by eye at each gate was rejected — it scales with the registry and fails silently as it grows.
AcceptanceCriteria: --strict exits 0 on a fully linked chain and 1 when any SR lacks an LLR/TC, any LLR/TC lacks a parent, or any SN lacks an SR; the orphan list names each at-fault id.

Title: Integrity floor for ids and CSV structure
Requirement: trace.py shall fail --strict-integrity on a duplicated or malformed registry id, a data row whose column count differs from its header, or a TC that pairs an LLR with an SR it does not decompose.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 — a misaligned or duplicated id corrupts the join before the orphan rules can notice, so the report is confidently wrong rather than red, and an incoherent SR/LLR citation contradicts the LLR's own parent link, leaving two answers to one question. Checking only at a gate was rejected: these are wrong the moment they are written, and a gate-only check lets a broken join sit in the tree for days.
AcceptanceCriteria: --strict-integrity exits 1 on a duplicate/malformed SR/LLR/TC/PB/REPO/MOD/PART/ASSET/CMP/IF id, a mis-columned row, or an incoherent SR/LLR pairing in one TC, and 0 otherwise; orphans do not affect it. MOD is the legacy compatibility id for current REPO rows.

Title: Placeholder and schema checks
Requirement: trace.py shall, under --no-placeholders, flag any leftover -000 example row, and under --strict-schema, require non-empty required fields and in-vocabulary Verification/Tier values.
Rationale: Realizes SN-022 (a committed placeholder at a gate is a finding) and SN-002 (a real row missing a required cell breaks the trace).
AcceptanceCriteria: --no-placeholders reports every -000 row across SR/LLR/TC and the SN doc; --strict-schema reports an empty required field or an out-of-vocabulary Verification/Tier value.

Title: Acceptance-criteria advisory
Requirement: trace.py shall warn (never fail) when an SR AcceptanceCriteria uses a comparative term with no pinning predicate in the cell.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 by keeping acceptance criteria testable, while leaving the call to the G1 review — a heuristic lint must not gate.
AcceptanceCriteria: A comparative claim with no pinning predicate marker emits a stdout WARNING and a report line; the exit code is unchanged.

Title: Off-spine registries stay traceable
Requirement: trace.py shall integrity-check the optional off-spine registries (PB/REPO/PART/ASSET, plus legacy MOD compatibility) and validate their back-links without blocking a project that does not use them.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 (off-spine rows stay linked to the spine) and SN-012 (an unused optional registry costs nothing — its -000 row is ignored).
AcceptanceCriteria: A PB row whose Refs name no real SR/LLR/Module, or a REPO row (including a legacy MOD row) delegating an unknown SR, is a finding; a -000 example row in any of them is ignored.

Title: Gate/tier harness enforces required steps
Requirement: check.py shall run the active gate's required steps and fail the gate when a required tool is missing, reporting SKIP(missing) rather than silently passing.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 (gates enforce their bar), SN-008 (no false green) and SN-014 (a missing tool fails, never skips). The work-branch lane skip is SR-133's obligation (one row, one obligation).
AcceptanceCriteria: check.py --gate GN runs that gate's steps; a required-but-absent tool fails the gate with guidance (never a silent pass), and --lenient degrades it to SKIP; --tier selects the declared step subset.

Title: Declared stack profile
Requirement: check.py shall read the toolchain (format/lint/test commands, tiers, coverage, arch-map mode) from docs/stack.ini so a stack swap edits only that file.
Rationale: Realizes SN-003 — the kit is stack-agnostic; the harness is re-pointed by declaration, not by editing a kit script.
AcceptanceCriteria: check.py resolves each step's command from stack.ini; changing the profile changes the commands run, with no script edit.

Title: Profile validation fails loudly
Requirement: check.py shall fail loudly on a malformed stack.ini, a non-integer coverage threshold, or a missing declared binary, rather than proceeding on a bad profile.
Rationale: Realizes SN-003 and SN-008 — a broken declaration is a red, never a silent misconfiguration.
AcceptanceCriteria: A malformed profile, non-integer coverage, or missing binary produces a clear nonzero failure at the relevant step.

Title: Conditional scaffold profiles
Requirement: bootstrap.py shall seed only the artifacts a chosen profile uses, omitting Python-only files for a non-Python stack.
Rationale: Realizes SN-003 (portability) and SN-012 (right-sizing — a repo gets only what it uses).
AcceptanceCriteria: A non-Python profile omits Python-only artifacts and seeds files-mode arch-map; a profile that selects no opt-in layers seeds none of them.

Title: Scaffold runs green out of the box
Requirement: bootstrap.py shall produce a scaffold whose harness runs green immediately after generation.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 (a working process without hand-building tooling) and SN-007 (the suite bootstraps a real scaffold and exercises every script).
AcceptanceCriteria: bootstrap.py --dest produces a scaffold on which the harness passes; the meta-suite runs every script against that scaffold.

Title: Idempotent re-runnable scaffold
Requirement: bootstrap.py shall skip an existing file on a re-run unless --force is passed.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 (safe drop-in onto an existing repo) and SN-007 — an adopter picking up kit updates must not lose their own edits, and a scaffolder that overwrites cannot be run twice, so it stops being run at all. Overwrite-always with a backup copy was rejected: it leaves the repo carrying a second copy of every file it touched. The deliberate kit-vs-project merge is a separate, operator-driven process (SR-036).
AcceptanceCriteria: A re-run leaves every existing file (kit- or project-owned) byte-unchanged without --force; --force overwrites.

Title: Doc navigability
Requirement: check_docs.py shall fail on a broken intra-repo link or a missing PROJECT-VISION tag, and check generated-doc freshness under --stale.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 — documentation stays navigable and honest; a broken link or undeclared vision is a red.
AcceptanceCriteria: check_docs.py --stale fails on a dead intra-repo link or absent PROJECT-VISION tag and passes a clean doc set.

Title: Runtime-flows check
Requirement: check_flows.py shall validate that the authored runtime-flow docs conform to their contract.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 — a hand-authored flow doc that drifts from its contract is caught.
AcceptanceCriteria: check_flows.py passes a conformant flow doc and fails a malformed one.

Title: Perf comparator and budgets
Requirement: check_perf.py shall compare a run against declared budgets and fail when a metric regresses beyond its tolerance.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 (a measurable gate bar) and SN-012 (perf is an opt-in layer).
AcceptanceCriteria: A metric within tolerance passes; one beyond its budget's tolerance fails at the declared block/warn level.

Title: Performance-budget back-links
Requirement: The performance-budgets registry (PB-###) shall keep every row's Refs resolvable to a real SR/LLR/Module.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 — the off-spine budget rows stay traceable to the spine.
AcceptanceCriteria: A PB row with an unresolvable or empty Refs is a finding; a resolvable one passes.

Title: No-stub detector
Requirement: check_stubs.py shall detect stub/placeholder markers in source at its declared gate and fail when one is present.
Rationale: Realizes SN-008 — a green never hides a stub.
AcceptanceCriteria: A stub/NotImplemented/pass-only public function at the declared gate fails; clean source passes.

Title: Always-on secrets floor
Requirement: check_privacy.py shall scan every commit's staged diff, message, and outgoing range for secret patterns regardless of the privacy toggle, unless docs/secrets-scan is explicitly set to off.
Rationale: Realizes SN-009 — a credential that reaches a shared branch must be treated as disclosed and rotated, and expunging it from history is a rewrite every clone has to follow, so the cheap moment to catch it is before the commit and the expensive one is any moment after. Folding the scan into the privacy toggle was rejected: that makes the highest-severity check opt-in alongside a preference. The one opt-out is an explicit declaration, so turning it off is a visible act.
AcceptanceCriteria: A staged PEM header, token, or key pattern is flagged and blocks; a clean diff passes; the floor runs with privacy-check off, and is disabled only by an explicit docs/secrets-scan: off.

Title: Privacy gate two-axis
Requirement: check_privacy.py shall add PII/identity classes when docs/privacy-check is on, exempting configured author identities.
Rationale: Realizes SN-009 — identity and PII classes are a policy choice a repo makes about its own contributors, unlike a leaked credential, which is a defect in every repo. Making them always-on was rejected because the exemption list they need is project-specific: a repo that has not declared its author identities would have the layer firing on its own commit metadata, and the fix would be to silence the scanner rather than to configure it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With privacy-check on, an identity/PII class is flagged unless the author is in EXEMPT_EMAILS; with it off, only the secrets floor runs.

Title: Pre-commit hook floor
Requirement: The pre-commit hook shall run the integrity + secrets floor on every commit, agent-neutrally.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005 and SN-009 — a floor only CI enforces is one the local tree crosses freely, and a secret caught after the commit is already in history. Trusting the agent to run the checks was rejected: a floor exists for the times the agent forgets, so it is git-enforced and agent-neutral.
AcceptanceCriteria: The hook runs trace --strict-integrity and the secrets scan on staged content and blocks a commit that fails either.

Title: Pre-push hook outgoing scan
Requirement: The pre-push hook shall scan the outgoing commit range and block a push that publishes a secret or (under privacy-check) a private identity.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005 and SN-009 — the last gate before content leaves the machine.
AcceptanceCriteria: The hook scans the push range and blocks when a secret (always) or an identity/PII class (privacy-check on) appears.

Title: Hook python probe
Requirement: The git hooks shall locate a working python3 by running a candidate and skip-or-report clearly when none resolves or a Store-alias exits nonzero.
Rationale: Realizes SN-013 — no cryptic crash when the interpreter is absent or a Windows Store alias.
AcceptanceCriteria: With no working python3 the hook reports clearly and does not crash; with one, it runs the checks.

Title: Vendored-doc drift
Requirement: check_vendored.py shall detect a vendored copy of an upstream doc drifting from its source.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 — a stale vendored doc is caught, not silently trusted.
AcceptanceCriteria: A drifted vendored copy is a finding; an in-sync copy passes.

Title: Arch-map generation
Requirement: gen_arch_map.py shall regenerate the symbol map inside its marker block and, under --check, fail when the committed map has drifted from source.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 and SN-021 — a generated view cannot silently rot; --check makes drift a red.
AcceptanceCriteria: --check fails when the map is stale and passes when current; regeneration rewrites only the marker block.

Title: Permutation case generation
Requirement: gen_cases.py shall expand a Permutations spec into concrete dimensional cases.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 — dimensional coverage is generated from the SR's declared inputs, not hand-listed.
AcceptanceCriteria: A spec grammar (range/set/bool with @full|@pairwise|@boundaries) yields the expected case set.

Title: Skills index + checked per-agent fan-out
Requirement: gen_skills_index.py shall regenerate skills/INDEX.csv from each SKILL.md applicability frontmatter.
Rationale: Realizes SN-012 (opt-in accelerators) and SN-021 — a hand-maintained index drifts from the skills it indexes, and an index that disagrees with its sources is worse than none, because it is trusted. Requiring each author to update the index by hand was rejected for the same reason the traceability matrix is generated: the discipline fails silently.
AcceptanceCriteria: The regenerated INDEX.csv reflects the current SKILL.md frontmatter, and a drifted index is detectable.

Title: Coordinator resumes headless
Requirement: agent_loop.py shall resume headless with stdin closed, never blocking on a prompt. Resume authority (one path - the serial resume loop is retired): a worker resumes from its explicit claimed assignment plus the committed trailer evidence on its branch, and the integrator (SR-132) derives claim/queue state from trunk history alone; docs/status.md is a generated reference surface (SR-059), never a session input.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006 and SN-016 — an unattended run blocked on a prompt is indistinguishable from a hung one and holds its lane until a human notices. Keeping a separate serial resume path beside the dispatcher was rejected: two authorities over one decision drift, and the divergence surfaces as a run that resumes differently depending on how it was started.
AcceptanceCriteria: A worker reconciles from its assignment + committed evidence and the integrator from trunk history; every mode runs with stdin closed and a prompt cannot wedge it.

Title: Coordinator preflight
Requirement: agent_loop.py shall refuse a broken footing in preflight — not a git repo, no agent CLI, or a private author under privacy-check — exiting a typed nonzero code rather than hanging.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006 and SN-015 — a run that starts on a broken footing fails later and further from the cause, and an unattended loop cannot be asked what went wrong. Continuing with a warning was rejected: each of these conditions makes every subsequent step meaningless, so a typed nonzero exit is what lets the caller act on it.
AcceptanceCriteria: Outside a git repo, with no agent CLI, or with a private author under privacy-check, preflight exits a typed nonzero code.

Title: Coordinator typed outcomes
Requirement: agent_loop.py shall end each session in a typed outcome code, guard a zero-commit HEAD, and report an all-ERROR stall as an unavailable agent rather than a work stall.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006, SN-019 and SN-020 — a coordinator ending in an untyped code forces its caller to parse prose; a session that produced no commit still has a HEAD to report, so without a guard an empty run is indistinguishable from a productive one in the record it leaves; and an all-ERROR run reported as a work stall sends a human looking for a blocked work item that does not exist. Treating an agent error as a stall was rejected for that reason: an unreachable agent and a blocked item need different responses, so they need different outcomes.
AcceptanceCriteria: A repo with no commits does not crash the loop; an agent-CLI error is logged ERROR; an all-ERROR region is reported as an unavailable agent.

Title: Coordinator lock auto-release
Requirement: The per-worktree coordinator lock shall be a kernel advisory lock the OS releases on process death, leaving no stale-pid wedge.
Rationale: Realizes SN-017 — the dispatcher, each worker and an interactive sitting all take this lock, so a holder that dies without releasing it wedges every one of them behind an entry nobody can safely clear. A pid file plus a liveness check was rejected because it cannot decide the case it exists for: if the pid has been reused the check sees a live process and keeps a dead lock forever, and if it guesses the other way it clears a lock that is still held. A kernel advisory lock releases on process death by construction, so the question never arises.
AcceptanceCriteria: After the lock holder dies, the next run acquires the lock; no stale-pid file blocks it.

Title: Second coordinator refused
Requirement: agent_loop.py shall refuse a second coordinator in the same checkout, preventing a two-writer race.
Rationale: Realizes SN-018 and SN-006 — two coordinators in one checkout write the same working tree, and the loser's commits interleave into the winner's diff where no review will separate them. Coordinating by convention was rejected: the failure is silent and shows up only as a garbled history.
AcceptanceCriteria: A second coordinator on a held lock is refused; only one writer runs per checkout.

Title: Declared-policy readers agree
Requirement: The gate-policy, push-policy, and privacy-check readers shall share one declared-value parse so the hooks, agent_loop, and check_privacy agree on the value.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 (policies drive the gate) and SN-005 (one source, every enforcer reads it the same way).
AcceptanceCriteria: The gate-policy and push-policy readers return the first declared line; every enforcer reads the same value.

Title: Onboarding and dev-setup scaffold
Requirement: The onboarding and dev-setup templates shall scaffold and run to a green developer setup.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 — a new contributor who cannot reach a working setup from the repo alone is blocked on whoever set it up last, and onboarding prose that is never executed drifts from the commands that work. A README checklist was rejected: nothing fails when it goes stale.
AcceptanceCriteria: The scaffolded onboard/dev-setup scripts run to a green setup.

Title: Release checklist generation
Requirement: gen_release_checklist.py shall emit the release-gate checklist, including the warn-tier performance budgets that never fail a gate.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 — the release gate has a generated checklist surfacing the budgets a human must tick off.
AcceptanceCriteria: Running the generator emits the checklist content: the perf-budget section lists each warn-tier PB with its id and allocation.

Title: Scripts are stdlib-only
Requirement: Every kit script shall run on a clean Python 3.11+ with no pip installs (standard library only).
Rationale: Realizes SN-011 — the kit imposes no dependency stack on a downstream repo to run its checks.
AcceptanceCriteria: No kit script imports a third-party package; an AST scan asserts every top-level import in scripts/*.py resolves to stdlib or a local sibling.

Title: Stack-agnostic across OSes
Requirement: The process and ID scheme shall be stack-agnostic.
Rationale: Realizes SN-003 — a method that presumes one language is re-derived by every adopter on a different stack, and the re-derivation is where the traceability guarantees get dropped. Shipping per-stack variants was rejected: it multiplies the surface that must stay consistent.
AcceptanceCriteria: The ID scheme is language-neutral.

Title: Deliberate re-sync integration
Requirement: A re-sync of an existing adoption shall integrate relevant kit updates without clobbering the adopter's filled-in files, per ADOPTING.md section 6 — take kit-owned scripts/hooks wholesale, regenerate generated docs, and preserve filled-in registries/config.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 and SN-007 — picking up kit updates is a deliberate diff-and-merge, not a mechanical operation: bootstrap.py supplies the docs/kit-version stamp and --force (SR-011), while the operator makes the overwrite-vs-preserve call, aided by the downstream-resync skill.
AcceptanceCriteria: Following ADOPTING.md section 6 against the docs/kit-version diff, kit-owned files are taken wholesale, generated docs regenerated, and filled-in files preserved.

Rationale: Preserves the stable ratified id and its attestation history while removing composite implementation obligations.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every listed target resolves; the supersession graph is acyclic; no LLR decomposes this row; TC-099 inspects the frozen migration map.

Rationale: Preserves the stable ratified id and its attestation history while removing composite implementation obligations.

Title: Duplicate-code lint
Requirement: check_dupes.py shall report any window of at least a configurable minimum of consecutive significant source tokens appearing at more than one location, and exit nonzero unless the finding's block fingerprint plus file pair (or a legacy bare file pair) is recorded in the census.
Rationale: Realizes SN-008 — the one-fact-one-home rule holds for prose because a reviewer reads prose; nothing reads code for it, so duplication accumulates until a fix must be applied in places nobody can enumerate. A review-only convention was rejected as unenforceable at scale. Opt-in at the product layer so a non-adopter pays nothing. Block-fingerprinted, count-aware exemptions are the preferred form because they let NEW copy-paste inside an already-listed pair fail; the coarser legacy file-pair exemption does not, which is the cost of accepting one.
AcceptanceCriteria: A copy-pasted helper across two files exits 1 naming both file:line locations; clean source exits 0; raising --min-tokens above the block's length passes; a docs/dupes-allow fingerprint+pair line suppresses that block while a new distinct block in the same pair still fails; --emit-census regenerates the lines.

Title: Per-phase routing and review dial
Requirement: The unattended coordinator shall select the agent command template per in-process session phase (PLAN/BUILD/REVIEW-A/REVIEW-B/DESIGN-CHECK/CRITIQUE - the coordinator's own activity; the retired docs/run-phase file, deleted by SR-059, is not an input) via AGENT_CMD_MAP/--cmd-map, falling back to the single AGENT_CMD; surface the declared reviewer dial (docs/review-policy, default 1) at run start without enforcing it; and warn (never block) when a lane resume surface exceeds the declared size threshold.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006 and SN-016 — two samples of one model share blind spots, so a review by the family that built the change agrees with it for the wrong reasons; cross-family routing is what makes the second opinion independent, and one model for every phase was rejected on that basis. Dispatch stays keyed off the in-process session phase because the alternative, a per-phase code branch, makes adding a phase a code change and so discourages adding one. The resume surface's growth tripwire warns rather than fails because a growing resume surface is a smell and not a defect, and failing on a smell trains an operator to bypass the check.
AcceptanceCriteria: A mapped session phase invokes its own command template and the default template does not fire; a broken map entry fails preflight before iteration 1; the banner surfaces docs/review-policy; an oversized status.md warns on stderr while the run proceeds; AGENT_STATUS_WARN_BYTES=0 silences.

Title: Doc reference validation
Requirement: check_doc_refs.py shall flag a documentation reference to a repository path that does not exist and an asserted sym:<module>.<name> reference missing from the generated module-map inventory, warn-first (exit 0) with --strict gating; absent inventory skips the symbol tier cleanly.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 and SN-008 — link resolution sees a broken link but not prose naming a file that was renamed away, nor an asserted code symbol that no longer exists; both read as correct forever. Validating every backticked word was rejected as unaffordable in false positives, so only path-shaped tokens and an explicit sym: convention are checked, generated marker blocks are exempt, and a path-ok line is the escape hatch for prose that names a path deliberately absent from the tree.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backticked repo path that does not exist warns and gates only under --strict; URLs, globs, placeholders, generated blocks and path-ok lines are ignored; a dangling sym: reference is flagged against the module map; with no inventory the symbol tier skips and the path tier still runs.

Title: OKF knowledge-bundle export
Requirement: gen_okf.py shall export the spine registries AND the key process docs as a generated Open Knowledge Format bundle under docs/okf — one typed markdown concept per real row (graph as resolvable markdown links, per-tier indexes) plus a Process Guide concept per present process doc (a summary derived from that doc and a resource pointer to the unmodified source) — deterministic (no clocks), with --check failing on any stale, missing or extra bundle file; docs/okf-export off silences and placeholder-only registries are vacuous.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 and SN-012 — traceability and process knowledge held only in this repo's own formats cannot be read by anything else, so the knowledge is trapped in the tool that produced it. The export is emit-only and stdlib-only, adding no runtime dependency and no parser: introducing a parser was rejected because reading the format back would make the bundle a second source of truth that can drift from the registries, whereas a derived bundle can only be STALE, which --check detects. Leaving the source docs untouched keeps the export non-intrusive, and the dashboard's Knowledge tab (SR-038) is its first consumer, so the bundle has a reader rather than being written for nobody.
AcceptanceCriteria: One frontmatter-typed file per real SN/SR/LLR/TC row whose graph links resolve; a Process Guide concept for each present process doc carrying a summary derived from the doc (not hand-authored) with the source left unmodified; regeneration is byte-identical; --check trips on a registry OR doc edit, a missing bundle and a hand-added file; the write mode prunes extras; off and placeholder-only registries pass silently, and process guides emit only alongside a real spine.

Title: Subagent spawn gate
Requirement: A PreToolUse subagent-spawn gate shall, during an unattended run, refuse or defer subagent spawns per docs/subagent-gate (off|ask|deny; absent=off), honor a launcher-set SUBAGENT_GATE=allow override the model cannot set, and fail open on any error so a broken gate never wedges the tools.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006 (a walk-away run stays safe — bounded, supervised fan-out with the override held by the human, not the model) and SN-012 (opt-in: absent/off is a vacuous allow, so a non-adopter pays nothing). Supervision, not security — a model that can edit files can remove the hook (adapted from stop-subagent-fanout, MIT; spec docs/archive/INTEGRATION_PLAN.md Phase 4).
AcceptanceCriteria: With docs/subagent-gate: deny a Task/Agent spawn is refused (permissionDecision=deny, exit 2); ask defers to approval; off/absent and SUBAGENT_GATE=allow allow it; a non-spawn tool is not gated; a malformed payload fails open (allow) and is logged.

Title: Run capability menu
Requirement: The root run.cmd/run.sh/run.command launchers shall present every major capability an evaluator runs from a single declaration - one name = command line (plus an optional name.desc line) per capability in docs/stack.ini's [run] section - via a stdlib scripts/run_menu.py that reads it: no args gives a numbered interactive menu, run_menu.py <name> launches one directly with exit-code passthrough, and --list emits a stable name<TAB>desc machine listing (the agent surface); an absent or empty [run] section prints the no-launch-command-wired-yet guidance and exits 1; the launch command is declared once (the duplicated RUN_CMD is retired) and works on Windows and POSIX.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 - the evaluator's rungs make running the product never depend on recalling a command, and the capability set is now declared once in docs/stack.ini instead of hard-wired and duplicated across the platform launchers. A new SR formalizing the launcher surface, which previously existed only as process prose.

Title: Derived gate from artifact states
Requirement: derive_gate.py shall compute the active gate from the spine artifact states (SN section-state + SR/LLR/TC Status maturity) and cache it to docs/gate rather than accept a hand-set value, so a gate advances only when the mechanical states do. Three Status values are recognized case-insensitively: Draft (G0 + decomposition exemptions), Verified (G3), and Modified — a post-attestation amendment owing a re-attest, deriving G2 through the existing decomposed-unverified rung with no arithmetic of its own; the cached basis line carries modified=N beside drafts=N so the pending state never hides.
Rationale: SSOT applied to the gate itself (docs/specs/derived-gate-model.md): a hand-set marker can be bumped without the work; deriving it makes gate advancement mechanical (SN-004) and un-gameable (SN-008). The hybrid cache keeps the value readable on checkout; --check guards rot.
AcceptanceCriteria: derive_gate.py --print on the meta computes the per-phase gates from the current states (a Modified SR's phase reads G2 until re-attested); --check exits nonzero when a state change is not reflected in the cached docs/gate basis; the compared line includes the modified=N count.

Title: Process reference view

Title: Dashboard accessibility (rubric-adjudicated)
Requirement: PROJECT_STATE.html shall be operable and readable without a pointer or full color perception: every interactive element (tabs, expandable blocks, SVG nodes with detail panels) is keyboard-reachable and carries an accessible name (title/aria/visible text); no information is encoded by color alone (status/phase/type encodings carry a text or shape cue); text keeps readable contrast against its fill.

Title: Dashboard UI uniformity (rubric-adjudicated)
Requirement: PROJECT_STATE.html shall read as one system across its tabs and views: one type scale and spacing rhythm; one status/phase/type color vocabulary applied consistently wherever the same concept renders; uniform node, edge, legend, and detail-panel styling across the SVG emitters; the same interaction idiom (expand, hover, detail) wherever the same structure appears.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024 and SN-023 — how alike is alike enough is subjective at the margins, so cross-view coherence cannot be pinned to a threshold without pinning the wrong thing. It is adjudicated against a written rubric by an independent session rather than by the authoring build, because the build and its author share the assumptions that produced the output: a self-judged view is checked against the intent that made it, not against a reader meeting it cold.
AcceptanceCriteria: A fresh family-heterogeneous CRITIQUE session judging the generated dashboard against docs/rubrics/dashboard-uniformity.md (authored at [v3]-[g2]) returns APPROVE citing numbered anchors; type scale, color vocabulary, per-emitter node/edge/legend styling, and interaction-idiom consistency are each a rubric anchor.

Title: Dashboard usability (rubric-adjudicated)
Requirement: PROJECT_STATE.html shall support its core reading tasks with low friction: a first-time reviewer finds the project state, the next work, and how the parts connect, each within one tab switch; views default to a legible density (start-collapsed per the greater-than-3 rule) and reveal detail without losing context; labels stay readable at default zoom with no clipped or overlapping text.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024 and SN-023 — task-level usability is perceptual (is this findable, is this legible), so a test can confirm an element exists and not that a reader can use it. Acceptance is adjudicated against a written rubric derived from the stakeholder intent rather than from the test, because a test written by the builder encodes the builder's own idea of usable.
AcceptanceCriteria: A fresh family-heterogeneous CRITIQUE session judging the generated dashboard against docs/rubrics/dashboard-usability.md (authored at [v3]-[g2]) returns APPROVE citing numbered anchors. The RUBRIC is the acceptance instrument and the single home for which anchors are live: an anchor whose core has been bound to a test is retired there, and a verdict must not cite a retired anchor. This row therefore does not enumerate the live set - it would be a third copy of it, and the copy that goes stale. A clause of the requirement above that a test now holds is verified through the LLR/TC chain, which the registry already records, not by a verdict.

Title: Ingest and human-decision process loops
Requirement: The Process tab shall additionally render the project's two circular working loops as linked flow panels: (A) the intake loop - owner/agent intake -> triage into work items with spec detail -> the scheduler-derived ready frontier in the WI registry (docs/work/) -> build/review -> merge; and (B) the human-decision loop - open-items population (including the gate-ratification table) -> human review and ruling -> the log's Decisions record -> merge - with the LLM_Agent entry point rendered once and shared by both loops; each stage links to its canonical home (status.md, the WI registry (docs/work/), open-items.html, log.md); the panels stay data-derived where a canonical source exists, self-contained, byte-deterministic; a data-less repo renders byte-identically and --check freshness is unchanged.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 and SN-021 — the Process tab shows the artifact lifecycle, the resume loop and the slice cadence, but not how work ENTERS or how the human decides, which are the two circular flows that close the method's loop; without them a reader sees the machine and not the way into it. Title: Typed dual-plan state machine
Requirement: plan_round.py shall enforce the typed dual-plan state machine, spend ledger, one-repair and revision caps, position-swap agreement, and PAGE outcomes.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024;SN-006 by isolating one independently reviewable obligation formerly carried by SR-066.

Title: Allowlist-only dual-plan briefs
Requirement: plan_briefs.py shall assemble planner, critic, and arbiter briefs only from SR/IF registries and strict prompt-template filling.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024;SN-006 by isolating one independently reviewable obligation formerly carried by SR-066.
AcceptanceCriteria: Briefs contain allowlisted registry material, exclude status/log/self-assessment data, reject unknown or unfilled slots, and honor override then kit fallback.

Title: Dual-plan coverage-step adapter
Requirement: plan_coverage_step.py shall adapt mechanical coverage results into clean, implicated-repair, repeated-failure, and malformed round outcomes.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024;SN-006 by isolating one independently reviewable obligation formerly carried by SR-066.
AcceptanceCriteria: Exit 0 advances, first findings implicate and repair once, repeated findings page, malformed is distinct and fails closed, and report payload is captured.

Title: Stable dual-plan artifacts and WI filing
Requirement: plan_artifacts.py shall persist stable round artifacts and file selected queued child WIs with mapped predecessors and registry-valid fields.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024;SN-006 by isolating one independently reviewable obligation formerly carried by SR-066.
AcceptanceCriteria: Round ids and stage names are stable; selected rows receive sequential ids, mapped dependencies, empty Deliverables and valid specs/tiers; line endings and prior log content survive.

Title: Fresh-session dual-plan execution
Requirement: plan_runner.py shall run two planners, cross-critiques, bounded revisions, and position-swapped arbiters as fresh sessions and select only on true-plan agreement.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024;SN-006 by isolating one independently reviewable obligation formerly carried by SR-066.
AcceptanceCriteria: The complete round runs unattended with fresh session identities; runtime fallback is bounded; content agreement selects; position bias, missing rubric, or no route pages honestly.

Title: Dual-plan direct-path isolation
Requirement: The worker shall refuse a dual row on the direct path.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024 and SN-006 — a dual-plan row built by the direct worker skips the competing-plan round that is the whole reason it was marked dual, and the skip is silent. Letting the worker fall back to a single plan was rejected: it produces a plausible result that nobody knows was never contested.
AcceptanceCriteria: Direct workers reject dual rows and --dual-plan rejects non-dual rows.

Title: Dual-plan round disposition
Requirement: The --dual-plan round shall commit SELECT as a docs-only disposition (children filed as queued specs, validated atomically with their generated views) and surface PAGE per gate policy, never silently.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024 and SN-016 — a disposition split across commits can land half-applied, and halting every lane for one round's outcome throws away the parallelism for work the outcome does not touch. Applying the disposition per-lane was rejected: the registries are shared, so concurrent writers conflict on every one.
AcceptanceCriteria: SELECT files children that pass the registry validator; a PAGE preserves the round's evidence on disk.

Title: Spec-lifecycle close-side coherence
Requirement: check_trajectory.py shall flag a done WI whose SpecRef is non-empty and a live docs/specs file (scaffold README/-000 exemplars excluded) cited by no open WI, warning on every run and failing under --strict.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 and SN-012 — the open half of the spec-of-record lifecycle was enforced and the close half was not, so a repo accretes stale SpecRefs and orphan live specs (measured at 137 rows and roughly 60 files) until nobody can tell which spec is live. A prose close rule was rejected because it is the control that was already in place while that backlog accumulated: an unenforced rule is indistinguishable from no rule at the point it matters. Opt-in and vacuous on a fresh scaffold.
AcceptanceCriteria: A done row with a SpecRef and an uncited live spec each produce an R-F WARN with exit 0 on a plain run and exit 1 under --strict; a shared doc cited by any open (incl. deferred/blocked) WI stays clean; docs/specs README and -000 exemplars never flag.

Title: Per-module coverage floors
Requirement: check_coverage.py shall fail when a module listed in the coverage-floor census is below its declared per-module line-coverage percentage in the pytest-cov JSON report, or is absent from that report, so the global --cov-fail-under floor cannot hide a thin high-risk module; an absent report skips and an empty census is a no-op.
Rationale: Realizes SN-008 and SN-012 — one aggregate coverage number lets well-tested generators subsidize thin coverage at the security and process boundaries, so a green overstates confidence exactly where it matters most. Raising the single global threshold was rejected: it penalizes every module for the weakest one without ever naming it. Opt-in at the product layer, so a non-adopter pays nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: A module below its floor exits 1 naming it; a declared module absent from the report exits 1; all floors holding exits 0; no coverage report (e.g. the smoke tier) SKIPs; an absent or empty census is a clean no-op; a malformed floor line fails loudly.

Title: Kit-version stamp
Requirement: bootstrap.py shall stamp docs/kit-version with the kit commit SHA and date, marked -dirty on an uncommitted kit tree.
Rationale: Realizes SN-007 — without a recorded origin an adopter cannot tell which kit version they are on, so a re-sync degrades from a diff into a guess and the ADOPTING.md re-sync procedure has no baseline to diff against. Deriving the version from file hashes was rejected: it reports that something differs without saying from what.
AcceptanceCriteria: docs/kit-version records the kit SHA and date; a scaffold from an uncommitted kit tree is marked -dirty.

Title: Checked per-agent skill fan-out
Requirement: The per-agent skill copies (.claude/.gemini/.agents) shall be a checked, generated fan-out of the one neutral skills/ source.
Rationale: Realizes SN-021 — one skill maintained in three agent-specific copies rots into three different skills, and the copy an agent actually loads is the one nobody edited. Maintaining a single shared directory was rejected because each agent harness looks in its own path; the fan-out is forced, so the copies are generated and drift is a finding.
AcceptanceCriteria: A per-agent copy that diverges byte-for-byte from source is detectable and refreshed by one command.

Title: Dev-setup wires the process floor
Requirement: dev-setup shall wire the pre-commit process floor (core.hooksPath) from its baseline.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 — a process floor that needs a separate opt-in step is active only for the contributors who already knew about it, which is the reverse of what a floor is for. Documenting the git command was rejected: the floor then protects the rung the contributor read about rather than the one they actually run.
AcceptanceCriteria: After dev-setup the pre-commit floor is active without a separate setup step.

Title: Kit scripts run across the supported OSes
Requirement: The kit scripts shall run on Python 3.11+ across Linux, Windows and macOS.
Rationale: Realizes SN-011 — a script that works only where its author ran it turns portability into a defect the adopter finds, and the path, line-ending and locking differences that break it are invisible on a single platform. Testing one platform and reading the others by inspection was rejected: every one of those differences has been a real failure here.
AcceptanceCriteria: The CI matrix spans Linux, Windows and macOS on Python 3.11 and latest (3.x) and is green; macOS runs on current Python only — the 3.11 floor is a platform-agnostic language/stdlib guarantee already exercised on Linux and Windows, while macOS's job is OS-specific behavior (fcntl.flock, paths, git worktrees) that does not vary by Python version, so the macOS+3.11 cell is excluded as a redundant-coverage call, not a runner-availability workaround (3.11 has arm64 macOS builds).

Title: Deterministic ready ordering
Requirement: schedule.py shall order the eligible ready frontier deterministically by gate class, then Priority descending, then transitive downstream-dependent count descending, then remaining hard-path length descending, then WI id.
Rationale: Realizes SN-025 — a frontier that is correct but unordered lets two readers of the same registry dispatch different work, so a rerun stops being reproducible and a scheduling bug cannot be replayed. Ordering by WI id alone was rejected: it ignores the critical path, so the chain everything waits on gets picked last.
AcceptanceCriteria: Ordering is identical across --explain and --format json; Priority outranks downstream-dependent count within one gate class; simulate --jobs 1 matches the serial order.

Title: Generated status surface
Requirement: The trunk lane shall maintain docs/status.md's generated snapshot as a freshness-gated reference surface never written on a worker branch (trunk_step --regen; concurrency-restructure SS5.2). (The docs/run-state half of this row retired with the dispatcher at Phase 5.)
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 — an agent-authored status surface drifts from the state it reports and is trusted anyway, and a worker branch writing it makes the snapshot describe one lane instead of the project. Letting each worker append its own status was rejected: it produces a file that conflicts on every integration and reports no coherent whole.
AcceptanceCriteria: The status snapshot regenerates on the trunk after a merge and fails its freshness gate when stale; work branches skip the gate and never commit the artifact.

Title: Dashboard freshness check
Requirement: gen_trajectory.py --check shall fail on stale or missing output, the visible git-derived as-of stamp being excluded from stamp-only comparisons.
Rationale: Realizes SN-021 — a committed dashboard that nobody re-checks becomes a confident picture of a project that has moved on, and the as-of stamp changes on every commit, so comparing it would make the check cry wolf and get disabled. Regenerating on read was rejected: the artifact is committed so it can be read without the toolchain.
AcceptanceCriteria: Stale or missing output fails --check, and as-of behavior is stable in and outside Git.

Title: Critique closure ratchet
Requirement: check_trajectory.py shall warn when a Critique WI closes after CHANGES-REQUESTED without validation evidence changing.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006 — a changes-requested verdict followed by a close with nothing altered is how a critique becomes a formality, and nothing else in the harness can see that pattern. Hard-failing the close was rejected: the evidence sometimes lands outside the registries, so the check reports rather than adjudicates.
AcceptanceCriteria: The lax-closure case warns, while an approval or a TC, test or rubric delta stays silent.

Title: Contradiction-safe dual-plan dispatcher class
Requirement: schedule.py shall derive a contradiction-safe single-WI scheduling class from PlanMode.
Rationale: Realizes SN-024 — a row whose PlanMode and SafetyClass disagree has no correct lane, and guessing one dispatches contradictory work rather than surfacing the contradiction. Defaulting to the safer class was rejected: it hides a registry error that only a human can resolve.
AcceptanceCriteria: PlanMode derives a single-WI class, and a contradictory SafetyClass quarantines the row.

Title: PAGE maps through gate policy
Requirement: The --dual-plan single-shot round shall map a PAGE through gate policy, hard-gating a human only under attended policy and otherwise reaching the pause-free attention (STALL) end state.
Rationale: Realizes SN-016 — a PAGE that always stops for a human makes the unattended loop attended in practice, while one that never stops discards the judgement the round asked for. Two separate mappings for the dispatcher and the single-shot round were rejected: they drift, and the drift shows up as a loop that hangs on one path only.
AcceptanceCriteria: A PAGE preserves evidence and follows attended/autonomous policy (attended -> NEEDS-HUMAN exit; autonomous/single-ratify -> STALL exit, no human gate).

Title: Spine stand-alone rule
Requirement: trace.py shall fail under --strict when any spine row's normative text cites a work item or a process doc.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010 — a row that cites a work item is unreadable to the audience that matters most: a downstream adopter, or an agent, with none of this project's history, who must resolve an id they cannot see before they know what the system does. A process-doc citation fails differently and just as badly: a row that cites the rule it is obeying inverts the relationship, so amending the process silently changes what the row appears to require. Warning instead of failing was tried and rejected: a warn nobody must act on is how 43 such rows accumulated before anyone measured them.
AcceptanceCriteria: A WI id or a process-doc citation in an SR Title/Requirement/Rationale/AcceptanceCriteria, an LLR Title/Detail/Rationale, or a TC Method/Expected/Parameters exits 1 under --strict and names the registry, row and cell; a script name, artifact path, rubric or sibling spine id does not; pointer columns are out of scope.

Title: Requirement form: one testable obligation
Requirement: trace.py shall fail under --strict when a non-Draft requirement repeats its obligation keyword, uses a different modal in normative text, states an obligation with no actor, or uses an unfalsifiable or open-ended term.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 — when one row carries two obligations and only one holds, no id reports the failure, so the gate passes on a partially-met requirement. Undecidable wording fails differently and worse: an unfalsifiable adjective cannot be tested, so the row is signed on impression. Each rule is a LEXICAL proxy for a semantic property and is scoped to what it can actually decide — counting the obligation keyword catches the shape that recurred here and does not claim to find every multi-obligation row. A semantic check was rejected as out of reach for a stdlib checker, and a readability score was rejected as a proxy for the wrong property: it measures prose complexity, not whether a reader can tell what is binding.
AcceptanceCriteria: A second `shall`, a non-`shall` modal, an actorless `shall be <participle>`, an unfalsifiable term, an open-ended escape clause, or a `shall` in an LLR Detail exits 1 under --strict; a Draft row, a zero-`shall` row, `must` as a project's own obligation keyword, and a multi-clause AcceptanceCriteria do not.

Title: Paraphrase advisory
Requirement: trace.py shall warn (never fail) when an SR Rationale re-words its own Requirement, or an LLR Detail re-words its parent SR Requirement, past a declared word-overlap threshold.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 — a child that restates its parent adds a second home for one fact and no decomposition, so the trace grows a level without gaining information and a later amendment updates one copy. It warns rather than fails because the detector is word overlap: a short, correct Detail legitimately shares vocabulary with the requirement it decomposes, and gating on a heuristic with a large legitimate majority produces a check that gets scrolled past. The two relationships named are the ones where the parent is unambiguous; a general child-cell rule was rejected because 'the parent' is not well defined for the rest.
AcceptanceCriteria: An SR Rationale overlapping its own Requirement, or an LLR Detail overlapping its parent SR Requirement, past the declared threshold emits a stdout WARNING and a report line; the exit code is unchanged.

Title: Registry representation migration
Requirement: The kit shall provide a mechanical converter between the work-item registry's two homes - the docs/work/ spec folder (status = directory, TOML frontmatter, Deliverable in the body) and the legacy docs/requirements/work-items.csv - refusing any status outside the known vocabulary, any materialization into a non-empty target, and any conversion while an in-flight active/<branch>/ claim exists (conversion is a drained-stop operation), with the round-trip proven over the live registry before an authority flip.
Rationale: The 140-cell lesson: an unproven representation change is where a registry silently loses cells. The converter is the migration path every adopter of the folder home takes, and the single spec writer the filing seam reuses (concurrency-restructure spec, Phase 2).
AcceptanceCriteria: wi_convert --verify over a populated registry exits 0 reporting cell-exact equality; an unknown status refuses naming the row; folder->CSV->folder is parse-equal including a hand-filed spec with no order key; an in-flight claim refuses conversion by name.

Title: Serial trunk step compiles log fragments and regenerates authority
Requirement: A serial trunk step shall compile docs/log.d/ work-branch log fragments into docs/log.md in merge order derived from git history - validating every fragment before any write, rebasing relative links to the log's home, deleting compiled fragments, failing loudly at the first error and never committing.
Rationale: The §5.1/§5.2 shared-surface rules (concurrency-restructure): no work branch writes log.md, so hand-merged logs become unrepresentable; the one deliberately serial actor stays tiny, idempotent and fail-loud (§5.5). The artifact-regen half is SR-134's obligation (one row, one obligation).
AcceptanceCriteria: Two committed fragments compile in git-add order with links rebased docs/-relative and the fragments deleted; an uncommitted or malformed fragment blocks the whole batch with nothing appended; a fragment-free run is a clean no-op.

Title: Tracked pause drains claiming to a merged stop
Requirement: A tracked docs/work/pause file (TOML: reason, since) shall pause claiming - everything in flight finishes and integrates - read via pause_reason as the ONE pause home (the legacy untracked docs/pause half retired with the dispatcher at Phase 5), failing closed on malformation.
Rationale: §5.6: pause means stop claiming and drain to a merged stop - never a strand. The tracked form survives clones, its reason is diffable history, and unpausing is an auditable deletion commit; a broken pause file must still pause, loudly. The pending-surface render is SR-135's obligation (one row, one obligation).
AcceptanceCriteria: A tracked pause file pauses the coordinator via pause_reason under the unchanged None/''/reason contract; a malformed file pauses with the pinned loud placeholder; a stray legacy docs/pause file is inert.

Title: Local integrator: serial fail-closed merge queue
Requirement: The local integrator shall claim work via a serial trunk commit (queued spec to docs/work/active/<branch>/, branch cut from that commit, refused while docs/work/pause is present), merge each finished claimed branch --no-ff onto a candidate worktree with the trunk step folded into the merge commit, run the declared bar on the composed tree - refusing on a missing or empty check declaration and on any SKIP in the bar's own report - require the policy-dialed verdict artifacts with git-derived freshness, fast-forward the trunk only on green, and stop loudly on red.
Rationale: The §1.2 seam's default backend: serial => composed-tree gating by construction; fail-closed against the dispatcher's recorded fail-open (a skipped bar merged 8 trains with zero gate-verified). Verdict freshness is git-derived because the WI-scoped §5.4 naming dropped the sha7 filename binding - without it a stale APPROVE clears the gate.
AcceptanceCriteria: A claim moves the spec and cuts the branch in one serial trunk step and is refused when paused, dirty, name-unsafe, not-ordinary or not-ready; a finished branch is detected from its tree alone; an absent or stale or CHANGES-REQUESTED verdict refuses the merge; a missing stack.ini or empty [product] test refuses; a red bar parks the candidate and stops the queue; the RULING-6 window audit flags a non-merge product commit.

Title: Work-branch lane skip for freshness steps
Requirement: On a claimed work branch (one whose history holds a docs/work/active/<branch>/ claim) check.py's generated-artifact freshness steps shall SKIP with a stated trunk-lane reason - generated artifacts are trunk-only - while every non-freshness step still runs.
Rationale: The skip is not a weakening: a work branch cannot commit generated artifacts at all (concurrency-restructure §5.2), so demanding their freshness there would force the very conflict the rule deletes; the skip is reported, never silent, and any signal ambiguity resolves toward the full trunk bar. Decomposed from SR-006 so each row states one obligation.
AcceptanceCriteria: on a claimed work branch the declared freshness steps SKIP with a §5.2 notice and exit code untouched while skills-sync, trajectory and registry-integrity still run; the closing commit and its successors keep the skip (the signal derives from branch history, not the working tree); the trunk lane never skips them.

Title: Trunk step regenerates the declared artifacts in dependency order
Requirement: The serial trunk step shall regenerate the declared generated artifacts in dependency order - the derived gate before its consumers - failing loudly at the first error and never committing.
Rationale: Stale-artifact merge conflicts become unrepresentable when only the serial trunk actor regenerates (§5.2/§5.5); dependency order because docs/gate is an input to the dashboard and status views, not an output. Decomposed from SR-130 so each row states one obligation.
AcceptanceCriteria: --regen skips absent artifact families with a notice and stops loudly at the first failing generator; derive_gate runs before the dashboard/status/open-items regens.

Title: Pending surface renders the declared pause verbatim
Requirement: The generated pending surface shall render a declared pause's since and reason verbatim - no clock - clearing when the pause file is deleted.
Rationale: An open pause is a visible accruing cost, never a forgotten one (the stale-reason lesson). Decomposed from SR-131 so each row states one obligation.
AcceptanceCriteria: the pending block renders Paused since <date> - <reason> with the declared date verbatim (no clock), omits the stamp when since is empty, renders the pinned fail-closed placeholder on malformation, and clears when the file is deleted.
